text:
Ivy: quick design thread — uploaded a compact compare slice: https://redwood.mock/compact/strip. Two decisions: collapse filter chips into a single summary pill vs keep separate chips, and how to show perf badges without confusing non-technical users.
Noah: Separate chips for scanability. If we must collapse, do it after 4 and use a focusable '+N' trigger that lists filters.
Sam: Agree. +N must be keyboard reachable and announce contents via aria-live. Also, don't bury the pin action — make it inline next to the version.
Priya: Microcopy: for badges surface numeric value with unit ("120 ms") and a tiny label like "typ.". Tooltip contains the stats: "p50: 120ms; p95: 420ms; n=1,240". Avoid showing p50 on surface.
a11y-bot: Accessibility notes: +N trigger should have aria-haspopup="listbox" and aria-expanded toggled. When the list opens, move focus to first item and populate an aria-live="polite" region with items. Pin toggle should use aria-pressed and have an accessible label: "Pin version for project". Ensure badge capsules meet contrast (4.5:1) at small sizes or include an icon so color isn't the only cue.
Ivy: Action items: (1) keep separate chips up to 4 then collapse into a keyboard-accessible +N; (2) badge surface -> "120 ms" + microtag, tooltip with p50/p95/n; (3) pin inline with explicit copy in modal: title 'Pin model version for project' and show Version ID + fallback note; (4) accessibility fixes per bot.
Noah: I'll update Figma and add keyboard flows. Sam: can you mock the pin modal copy?
Sam: will do, dropping link when ready. :thumbsup:
Ivy: thanks — aiming to have Figma + copy by EOD for sprint planning.
